us.h: Nor'easter cuts power to 400,000-plus on Thanksgiving morning
us.s: More than 400,000 people lacked power Thursday morning, about 150,000 in Virginia. New York and New Jersey declared emergencies; peak coastal flooding hits at the morning high tide, with 60–70 mph gusts possible into Friday.

us.h: Second judge blocks Trump's revised birthright citizenship order
us.s: D.C. federal judge Christopher Cooper barred State, DHS and Social Security from enforcing the August order against a certified class of children, citing Supreme Court precedent. A Maryland judge had already blocked it in September.

us.h: Judge bars FCC from early review of ABC licenses
us.s: Judge Loren AliKhan found the FCC's accelerated look at ABC station licenses was likely unconstitutional retaliation for speech, citing Trump's repeated calls to pull them, and issued a preliminary injunction. ABC hailed a First Amendment win.

us.h: Trump calls Huang pardon 'an option'; Vance says unnecessary
us.s: Ahead of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Capitol Hill appearances over chip exports to China, Trump said a pardon remained possible but likely not needed. Vance said he has seen no evidence Huang committed a crime.

world.h: Iran says two more tankers hit mines in Hormuz
world.s: Revolutionary Guards claim two tankers, including a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels, exploded near Oman's Khasab after taking an 'unauthorised' route. Iran vows to keep the strait closed despite US Navy escorts.

world.h: China, allies push back on new US tariff plan
world.s: Beijing called the overcapacity rationale a false premise and promised countermeasures; Japan, Singapore, Malaysia and the EU also objected. Proposed duties of 15-35% would likely start in early 2027.

world.h: Congo Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 confirmed cases
world.s: Described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, nearly half of confirmed cases have died. Renewed rebel-army fighting near Bunia is blocking response teams and leaving treatment centers short-staffed.

world.h: EU leaders clash over budget and Ukraine loan
world.s: At a Brussels summit, leaders are split over a nearly 1.7 trillion euro seven-year budget and a proposed 45 billion euro jointly financed loan for Kyiv, which several Central European states want to skip.

world.h: US-led group strikes deal for Lukoil's foreign assets
world.s: A consortium led by Todd Boehly's Eldridge, including the US development finance agency, would swap Lukoil securities for its overseas oil fields and stations, about 350,000 barrels daily. Treasury sanctions officials must still approve.

world.h: Explosion and fire hit Bangkok oil depot
world.s: A blast at Bangchak's depot in eastern Bangkok injured several people and prompted evacuation orders nearby; the company shut its Phra Khanong refinery units. The fire was later brought under control.

tech.h: Nvidia reportedly halts AI server shipments to Southeast Asia
tech.s: Per the Financial Times, Nvidia told partners to stop server deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new US rules targeting Chinese firms renting Nvidia-powered cloud capacity.

tech.h: FCC approves SpaceX's million-satellite orbital data centers
tech.s: The FCC cleared 'Starmind,' up to 1 million data-center satellites, overriding objections from Amazon, Viasat and astronomers. First satellites are due by 2033; Musk targets a 2027 launch.

tech.h: 42 states fight Character.AI sale of user chats
tech.s: State attorneys general intervened in Character.AI's bankruptcy to block auctioning chat histories from 21 million-plus US accounts, including over 2 million minors. The auction is set for December 1.

tech.h: Researcher says MiniMax user data accessed by unknown parties
tech.s: A Dragos researcher found secret links sent to Chinese AI firm MiniMax were later opened from Beijing, Shanghai and Singapore, despite no-retention requests. MiniMax says its security scanner opened links and denies disclosure.

talking.h: Storm postpones Macy's parade for first time ever
talking.s: The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade moves to Saturday at 8:30 a.m. because of the coastal storm, the first weather postponement in its history. NYC's mayor warned of 65 mph gusts and possible flash flooding.

talking.h: Rams top Packers in first Thanksgiving Eve game
talking.s: Los Angeles beat Green Bay 26–13 on Netflix behind Blake Corum's career-high 184 rushing yards, while Jordan Love threw two interceptions. Thursday's NFL tripleheader follows, capped by a Mahomes–Allen matchup.

talking.h: Online holiday spending running 9% ahead of last year
talking.s: Adobe says shoppers spent over $82.5 billion online Nov. 1–22, up 9.1%. It expects $6.9 billion today, $12.9 billion on Black Friday and $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday.

coming.s: After a full Thanksgiving closure, NYSE and Nasdaq close at 1 p.m. ET Friday; bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

coming.h: Rescheduled Macy's parade steps off Saturday
coming.s: The postponed 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is set for Saturday at 8:30 a.m. in Manhattan.

coming.h: Cyber Monday expected to be biggest online day
coming.s: Adobe forecasts $15.1 billion in U.S. online spending on Cyber Monday, up 6.2% from last year.
Jensen Huang is due on Capitol Hill Dec. 1 and 3, as sole witness before Senate Banking plus closed-door House committee sessions.

coming.h: FAA, Duffy face Congress over nationwide ground stop
coming.s: FAA chief Bryan Bedford testifies to a House panel Dec. 1 and Transportation Secretary Duffy to a Senate subcommittee Dec. 2 about the Nov. 13 outage and his $50 billion modernization request.
BLS releases the November employment report Friday at 8:30 a.m. ET; October job openings (JOLTS) come Tuesday, Dec. 1.
